text:
Anya: observed p99 spike on hosted API for model 'redwood-3b' around 07:18 UTC, looks like a backend queue/backpressure issue, tagging eng-runtime
Raj: seeing same, p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~250ms, p99 up to ~900ms for a burst window (07:18:00-07:20:30)
Anya: queue depth on serving pool 'hosted-gpu-eu' went from 6 -> 48 at peak, backlog correlated with a tenant that had many short requests with large prefixes
Diane: KV cache eviction rate spiked at 07:17:55, eviction/sec went from 50 -> 1.4k, suggest noisy prefix churn causing cache miss storms
Leo: batching telemetry shows average batch size collapsed from 16 -> 4 during the window, which increases per-token overhead
Jin: kernel selection logs show rapid kernel swap events around the same time, many fallback selections to 'generic-sm8' kernel at 07:18:05
Anya: can someone pull the kernel-selection trace? suspect mispredicted affinity heuristic leading to expensive kernels + smaller batches
perf-bot: kernel_selection_worker: sample flame: 60% kernel_selector::choose_kernel, 25% cuda_launch, 10% memcpy, 5% idle
Raj: flamegraphs attached in thread (summary below):
```
- kernel_selector hot path: heuristic::score_variant()
- fallback trigger: quantized mismatch + seq_len>256
- majority fallback picks were int8-generic kernels with higher latency
```
Diane: also saw NVLink stall counters rise, suggesting remote KV fetches increased due to cache misses
Anya: hypothesis: a mix of noisy tenant with long prefixes + our prefetch aggressor ramping caused cache churn -> more remote KV fetches -> kernel heuristic picks fallback kernels because runtime thinks model variant isn't friendly for cached KV flow
Leo: can reproduce locally: run load pattern with many short requests carrying 400-600 prefix tokens with random prefixes; we hit same kernel swap and batch collapse
Jin: quick profiling snippet I ran:
```
$ perf top -p <pid>
# shows kernel_selector and device wait stacks
nvlink_stalls: +420% during spike
```
Anya: immediate mitigations proposed: 1) set prefetch.concurrency=2 for hosted-gpu-eu 2) temporarily pin kernel_policy=prefer_fast for 'redwood-3b' on hosted pool 3) throttle tenant at rate limit gateway by 2x until rollout complete
Raj: applied prefetch.concurrency=2 at 07:25 UTC to one AZ, restarting few workers gracefully
ops-bot: config change applied: prefetch.concurrency=2 on pool hosted-gpu-eu-1 by Raj at 07:25:34 UTC
Leo: after prefetch change batch size recovered to ~12 and queue depth dropped to ~10, p95 back to ~140ms, p99 ~270ms within 2 minutes
Diane: pinned kernel_policy=prefer_fast on pool at 07:27 to avoid fallback churn, ops-bot confirmed
ops-bot: kernel_policy set to prefer_fast on pool hosted-gpu-eu-1 by Diane at 07:27:10 UTC
Jin: note this is a mitigation; root cause likely a regression in kernel scoring heuristics deployed in commit 0f3a2c7 on 2026-02-15 that changed pref thresholds for seq_len boundaries
Anya: created perf regression ticket: PERF-4823 referencing commit 0f3a2c7, marked P1, assigned to Raj
Raj: logs/metrics to attach to ticket: kernel-selection traces, kv-eviction rates, batch-size-time series, per-tenant request distribution, flamegraphs from perf-bot
perf-bot: suggested deeper profiling: collect GPU kernel timelines via nvprof for affected window, and heap snapshots of KV cache keys to see churn patterns
Diane: action items:
- Raj: investigate scoring change in 0f3a2c7 and add unit/regression tests for seq_len boundary (due EOD)
- Jin: run nvprof capture under synthetic noisy-tenant pattern and upload artifacts (due EOD)
- Leo: add alert rule for rapid KV eviction spikes (>500/sec sustained) and batch-size collapse (<8 for >30s) (due tomorrow)
- Anya: coordinate with infra to evaluate tenant move to dedicated pool if we see recurrence (ongoing)
Anya: next steps: follow-up postmortem if PERF-4823 surfaces code regression; if not regression, need tuning: reduce prefetch aggressor ramp, adjust kernel-scoring weight on cache-friendliness, and add an emergency autoscaling runway for queue depth spikes
Raj: quick note, rollback of 0f3a2c7 reproduces stable behavior in staging, so leaning toward code regression as root cause
Leo: adding canary that forces fallback-prob sampling to detect noisy tenants earlier
Anya: thanks all, marking thread for follow-up and I'll update on incident channel once PERF-4823 has a root-cause and patch plan
ops-bot: incident created INC-2026-089 by Anya at 07:33:01 UTC referencing thread 1990001111
Diane: tagging @support to inform affected customers we implemented mitigations and are investigating
Jin: uploaded nvprof artifacts to s3://perf-artifacts/1990001111/nvprof.tgz
Raj: assigned PERF-4823 to me and set milestone "fix-kernel-scoring-2026-03"
Anya: closing on-call loop, will keep monitoring for 2 hours and revert temporary kernel pins once patch is validated
Leo: preliminary blameless root cause: kernel scoring regression + aggressive prefetch ramp interacting with noisy prefix workloads -> cache eviction storm -> batch collapse -> p99 spike
Anya: end of thread for now, ping me with any new anomalies.
